key_points: A function assigns exactly one output to each input; the vertical line test checks this on a graph.
The domain is the set of inputs where f(x) is defined, and the range is the set of outputs f(x) takes.
A function is increasing on an interval when larger x gives larger f(x), and decreasing when larger x gives smaller f(x).
Even functions satisfy f(-x)=f(x) and are symmetric about the y-axis; odd functions satisfy f(-x)=-f(x) and are symmetric about the origin.
For a piecewise function, evaluate using the branch whose condition the input satisfies.
guide.explanation: The domain is the set of inputs where f(x) is defined, and the range is the set of outputs. A function is increasing where larger x gives larger f(x) and decreasing where larger x gives smaller f(x). It is even when $f(-x)=f(x)$ (symmetric about the y-axis) and odd when $f(-x)=-f(x)$ (symmetric about the origin). Source: Lecture1.pdf p.10, p.20, p.22-23.

questions.question: What is the domain of $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{x-1}$?
questions.explanation: The function is undefined when the denominator $x-1=0$, so $x\neq 1$ (Lecture1.pdf p.12).

questions.question: For $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{1-x}$ on the branch $x>1$, what is $f(2)$?
Using the absolute value function defined piecewise by $|x|=x$ for $x\ge 0$ and $|x|=-x$ for $x<0$, what is $|-4|$?
questions.explanation: Since $-4<0$, the rule $|x|=-x$ applies, giving $|-4|=-(-4)=4$ (Lecture1.pdf p.13).

questions.question: The function $s:\mathbb{R}^+\to\mathbb{R}$, $s(x)=\pi x^2$, has what range?
questions.explanation: For $x>0$, $x^2>0$ and so $\pi x^2>0$, and $x^2$ takes every positive value, so the range is $(0,\infty)$ (Lecture1.pdf p.12).

questions.question: Which relation is NOT a function of $x$?
questions.explanation: For $x=4$, $y^2=4$ gives $y=2$ or $y=-2$, so one input has two outputs and the vertical line test fails (Lecture1.pdf p.16).

questions.question: Which of these functions is even?
questions.explanation: Here $f(-x)=(-x)^2=x^2=f(x)$, so the function is even and symmetric about the y-axis (Lecture1.pdf p.22).

questions.question: Is $f(x)=x^3-x$ even, odd, both, or neither?
questions.explanation: $f(-x)=-x^3+x=-(x^3-x)=-f(x)$, so the function is odd and symmetric about the origin (Lecture1.pdf p.23).

questions.question: Is $f(x)=-3x+2$ increasing or decreasing on $\mathbb{R}$?
questions.explanation: The slope $-3$ is negative, and a negative slope means the linear function is decreasing (Lecture1.pdf p.41).

questions.question: In the linear blue whale model $W=3.51L-192$, what does the slope $3.51$ mean?
options: Each extra foot of length adds about 3.51 tons to the estimated weight
Each extra ton of weight adds 3.51 feet to the length
The estimated weight is 3.51 tons when length is zero
The estimated length is 3.51 feet when weight is zero
questions.answer: Each extra foot of length adds about 3.51 tons to the estimated weight
questions.explanation: In $f(x)=ax+b$, the slope $a$ is the increase in $y$ for a 1-unit increase in $x$. Here $W$ is in tons and $L$ is in feet (Lecture1.pdf p.28, p.35).
